get.description: The current story world with all its chapters (SPEC §13.3).

post.description:
One task done. Idempotent; judged by `judge_done` (404 unknown_task, 409
activities_closed / activity_locked / activity_too_old, SPEC §13.3, §14.4a). `attempts`
is stored for read and calc tasks (§14.2, §15.2). The first done row of a task earns its
stars (§14.4, +1 for read or calc right at the first try). Draw and write may still be
done without a photo (older apps, §15.3).

A photo of a drawing or a story (§15.3): raw JPEG body, at most 15 MB (413
photo_too_large). Only draw and write (422 photo_not_allowed). Judged exactly like `done`
(`done_at` = when the photo was taken), then the photo is stored (EXIF-rotated, without
any metadata, WebP lg/sm) and the task is marked done. A second photo of a done task is
stored too but earns nothing. 422 bad_image for a body that doesn't decode. World name
and task title are kept as snapshots in the story language (§14.7).

get.description: Settings, days off, the queue with its dates, worlds, the last 14 days, examples.

The done tasks (§17.2, §17.3), newest first, a page at a time: `before_id` = the
previous page's `next_before_id`.

delete.description:
Open again (§17.3): in one transaction, deletes the done row and its photo rows and
books a `reopen` row of -min(its stars, the balance), `ref_id` = the done id (none for 0),
so the balance never goes below 0. The photo files go after the commit (best effort: a
leftover file is harmless, a missing one for a kept row would not be). The tablet sees
the task open on its next refresh; its sticker goes with the chapter's last done task.
404 unknown_done.

post.description:
One bonus star per done task, every kind (§17.3): a ledger row `bonus`, +1, `ref_id`
= the done id; it counts as earned. Again -> 409 bonus_given; 404 unknown_done (checked
and written as one atomic step).

put.description:
The story queue. A new first world starts today; reordering later ones keeps the
dates of the running one (§13.2 rule 7). `langs` sets the story language of queued worlds
(§14.7); 422 lang_not_in_world for a language the world has no texts in.

Activity days (Mon=0), the unlock time, the child's level (§14.1) and the opening times
(§14.4a); level and windows omitted = kept. Dates of the current and later worlds are
recomputed from the queue start (§13.2 rule 6).

Deducts the wish's stars now; 409 not_enough_stars if the balance is too low (the
request stays pending). Decision, balance check and spending are one atomic step.

get.description:
The voice per language with its licence and attribution, and how many of the spoken
texts of all worlds are rendered, pending or failed (since the last start).
A rendered text, for the editor's play buttons (the `audio` URLs in WorldFull).

post.description: +N minutes or +N items on one rule, for today only (SPEC §3.5).

schema.title: Response Usage History Api Admin Usage History Get

post.description: Deletes today's plays and minutes (SPEC §3.5), e.g. as a reward.
Import one of the example packs (a folder, §13.5), like an upload.

put.description:
A story pack: a zip with world.json and pictures, or world.json alone (§13.5).
With dry_run=true it is only checked. An existing slug is replaced in place. Its spoken
texts are queued for rendering (§14.3).

delete.description:
Deletes the world, its done rows (FK cascade), cover and chapter pictures, and removes
it from the queue.

get.description: The world for the editor, with the audio of its rendered spoken fields (§14.3).

put.description:
Save the editor: texts, chapters, age band and colour. The slug can't change; the cover
and chapter pictures are set separately and stay by position (`cover`/`image` names in
the body are ignored, and so are the output-only `audio` maps). Changed spoken texts are
queued for rendering (§14.3).
A chapter's picture (raw image body, like the cover). 404 for an unknown chapter.

get.description:
The world as a pack zip (§13.4): world.json plus cover.webp and chapter-<n>.webp for
the pictures it has, so export -> import keeps them.

The whole file for the offline copy. Downloading is not playing, so no rule check
here; plays are counted when they happen (and synced via /play/batch).

Range streaming with the same rules as start/heartbeat (SPEC §5.3).

The item limit, the listening budget and the gems are skipped (ExoPlayer preloads
the next queue item before its start call, §16.2), and an active grace keeps the
playing item streamable through lockouts and minute limits (§3.3a). Admin previews
aren't rule-checked.

post.description: Exchange a single-use 6-digit code for a device token (SPEC §5.1, §7).

Offline plays, sent when the tablet is back online. Each event is booked once:
a retried batch (lost response, app restart) is de-duplicated by event_id.
Starting always goes through the normal rules; grace never starts a file (§3.3a).

get.description: Stars, the sticker album, the swaps and the wishes (SPEC §14.4).

post.description:
Stars for today's per-rule bonus (§3.5): an `adjustments` row plus a ledger row.
409 swap_limit_reached / not_enough_stars. Check and spend are one atomic step: two taps
at once can't both pass the balance check.

The child's "I'd like this": a pending request for the parent.
409 request_pending if one is open, 409 not_enough_stars if the balance is too low.
Atomic, and the partial unique index allows one pending request per wish anyway.

get.description: A rendered text (the `audio` URLs in GET /api/activities).
